paper:
In the oases of Adrar and Timimoun, in the Algerian Sahara, people have used an ancient system to bring water to their gardens for hundreds of years: the foggara. A foggara is a long underground tunnel which collects water from the ground and carries it slowly to the palm groves.

This clever system does not need any electricity or pump. It uses only the slope of the land. The water is shared fairly between the families thanks to a special stone with small holes. Each family receives a quantity of water according to its share.

Today, many foggaras are dry or abandoned because of new wells and the lack of maintenance. Experts say that if we don't protect them, an important part of our heritage will disappear. They also remind us that water is precious everywhere: we should save it at home and at school.

(Text written by the site)

Part One (14 points)

A. Reading comprehension (7 points)

1. True or false? a) Foggaras are found in the Algerian Sahara. b) A foggara needs electricity. c) Some foggaras are abandoned today.

2. Answer: a) What is a foggara? b) How is the water shared between families?

3. Who or what do the underlined words refer to? "it" (§1, line 3) → … ; "They" (§3, line 3) → …

B. Mastery of language (7 points)

1. Find in the text words closest in meaning to: old = … ; valuable = …

2. Find in the text the opposite of: quickly ≠ … ; unfairly ≠ …

3. Complete with the right form of the verb (conditional type 1): If we (to repair) the foggaras, the gardens (to stay) green.

4. Give advice using "should" or "shouldn't": a) leave the tap open while brushing your teeth. b) water plants in the evening.

5. Classify according to the pronunciation of final "ed": used – collected – watched – shared
